utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You would have observed that the chief of the victims and witnesses unit -- may I ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you just made a declaration to speak the truth and nothing but the truth, but prior to that you had answered many questions from me and from Mr. Alarid, and I want to find out from you whether when you gave those answers you were also speaking the truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The truth, the truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: For the purposes of the record, we'll treat her prior testimony as having been made subject to the declaration. Mr. Alarid, you may put certain questions to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, we're -- as you signed that pseudonym sheet, your -- I'm going to speak to you, and when I speak to you I may call you CW1 instead of your name to protect your identity. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm going to take my time because the interpreters need to finish interpreting to you, and then they need to finish interpreting to the Court, and so it goes a little slower. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I will further go slow because I'm going to turn my microphone on and off, so please wait after I speak so I can turn it off because then your voice will not go out over my channel, and that way it can remain protected.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then because this is a recorded transcript, and I know you're speaking very softly, but you'll need to speak loud enough and into the microphone so the interpreters can hear you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And before we get started, I really deeply want to apologise to you for bringing you here and opening wounds that you don't deserve to have opened at this late date, but I think you have some important evidence to say, but I'm very sorry for the pain this has caused you and the pain that you've carried with you all these years, and I will try and be sensitive to that at all times. And if I am not sensitive to that, you tell me, and I will correct myself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, looking at the list of alleged victims for the Pionirska Street fire as attached to the second amended indictment in this case, the first name is Mula Ajanovic. Do you know a Miss Mula Ajanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how do you know her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know her as a neighbor. I would see her. We would be visiting one another. I know her. Of course I know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And as far as you know, was she in Koritnik before you left on the 29th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: They were in Koritnik when I was in Visegrad. I don't know anything more. I mean, after -- other than for me -- or, I mean, about me, I don't know what else happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I only want you to know if you knew that they were, let's say, home in Koritnik but not necessarily -- I don't expect you to know anything after you left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I really don't know. I'm sorry. I don't know. I wasn't there. I was in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who is Adis Delija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Adis Delija is from Pionirska, from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you know who his mother is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Jasmina Delija.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 3, Ajnija Delija.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Ajnija Delija. That is Adis's grandmother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did she live in Koritnik or Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: In Visegrad, in Pionirska.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 4, Jasmina Delija, is that the Jasmina you just mentioned as number 2's mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what is Jasmina's maiden name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, what are you hoping to get from this? I would have thought that what was important was whether the witness was in a position to say whether any of these persons whom she knew before she left is alive now. Are you coming to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think in going through the list as you'll note one of the issues we've raised are deferentials between what we've discovered from Bosnia, what's been presented in the P119 and other lists in the case . And I think what you have here is you have a witness from the family that can explain the interrelationships, also assist the Court in understanding P119, which has a significant amount of data. It also goes to whether or not some of these people are actually people that should be on the list or did they ever exist. And that is important, as you have to weigh the evidence of her knowledge of the family as a whole as well as the people that are on the list that exist. And some of them, it would be my position that they're improperly referenced on the list by virtue of lack of supporting evidence given her testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If that's Mr. Alarid's case, then it seems there are two questions he can put to the witness. Are there any people that she has seen on this list that she knows never to have existed, that she does not know. And, two, does she see any names on this list that she has seen them since the 14th of June, 1992. I think we can save quite a bit of time by doing it in that fashion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree. I agree. I don't think you really need to use that roundabout method, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's not roundabout. It's actually pointed and specific in relation to the individual victims listed, and, Your Honour, it's my position that the state -- or the OTP has not met its burden with regards to the list given the totality of the circumstances, and this is my evidence, Your Honour. I'd like leeway to present my Defence, and I think that although it's going to take a while, it's not going to take too long going name by name as we've seen right now by the first three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let's move as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, number 5 on the list -- excuse me, number 4, Jasmina Delija, do you know who her mother is of the Kurspahic side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Besira Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And let's just -- moving to number 5, there was simply a Hasena, family name unknown, at this time. Did you know any Hasenas, either of Kurspahic family from Koritnik or other last names that might have been with the group from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Hasan Kurspahic had a daughter, Hasena, but she's alive in Bosnia somewhere. There was Edhem Kurspahic who had a daughter, Hasa. I don't know if her name is Hasa or Hasena. The name is quite unclear. I don't know. I don't know. I mean, I know one Hasena, Hasan's daughter. She's alive. I don't know if that is this Hasena or some other woman. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next, number 6, is Tima Jasarevic. Did you know her as someone who would have been from Koritnik or in the group from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe this witness can say who is in the group.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: All she can testify to whether she knows this person. She wasn't there at the time the Koritnik group was brought down to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll rephrase, Your Honour, just for the Prosecution's point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know a Tima Jasarevic from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know a Hajra Jasarevic from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know a Meho Jasarevic from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know a Mujo Jasarevic from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The next sheet, please. Can we have the next nine names from the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And looking at number 10 from the list, Aisa Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Aisa Kurspahic. There was a woman of that name, I know her, yes. I knew Aisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who was her father, and who was her husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know about the father. I don't know where she was born, but I know that her husband was Dzemail Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know number 11, Aida Kurspahic, approximately 12 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How do you know her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know her as a child.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you say whether she's alive now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was there, she was alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who is her mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Ismeta Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who was her father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Hidajit Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 12, Ajka Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know Kurspahic Ajka. She's Aida's grandmother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that would also be Ismeta's mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, mother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. And as far as you know, was she in Koritnik the 29th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not even sure that we've established that CW1 -- the evidence that I've heard is she was in Visegrad. So can we please clarify on what basis she would know who was in Koritnik on the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I think that's a fair statement of the evidence before the Court. The witness, I believe, said she hadn't been up to Koritnik for the week before, so that would be probably an improper question for me to ask considering it would cause for some speculation. So I won't ask that question anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, number 13 is Alija Kurspahic, approximately 55 years old. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Alija Kurspahic. That's a man. I know this person, and he stayed in Koritnik after I left. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 14, Almir Kurspahic, approximately 10 years old. Do you know this child?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Almir Kurspahic, the son of Ismeta Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did he also have a brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. His brother was Vahid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Redaction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when did -- was Aner Kurspahic alive on the 29th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: It's hard to say. I don't know. Up until 4.00, he was alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 16.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Kurspahic, Becar. I know him. He stayed after I left. He stayed in Koritnik after I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 17, Bisera Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Bisera Kurspahic is the mother of Jasmina Delija.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 18, Bula Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know Bula Kurspahic. She stayed in Koritnik after I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 19, Dzheva Kurspahic, approximately 22.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Dzheva Kurspahic is the daughter-in-law of Bula.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know who Dzheva's daughter and son are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: The daughter was Mirela, and the son was Ismet Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. And number 20, Enesa Kurspahic, approximately 2 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know her. It's the daughter of Mujesira Kurspahic. I know her as a small child.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And does she have a sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. Her sister was Halida.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 21, a Kurspahic whose first name was unknown but was a 2-day-old baby. Would there be someone that you might believe was this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I think that this was the grandchild of Aisa Kurspahic, the child of Sadeta Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. And number 22, Hasa Kurspahic, approximately 18 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, I know her. She remained in Koritnik after I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 23, Kurspahic Hajrija, approximately 60 years old but reported as a birth date in the Prosecution as 1914, date of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know. It could be a mistake. It could be Hajro Kurspahic, a man. I don't know of any Hajrija Kurspahic. I know of Hajro Kurspahic, and he had died of natural causes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When did he die of natural causes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there. I hadn't even gotten married then. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're saying he died before you got married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. He wasn't in the village when I came, but I believe it's Hajra. It's not Hajrija. I believe there's a mistake in the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 24, Kurspahic Halida, approximately 10 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, Halida Kurspahic, daughter of Mujesira Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 25, Hana Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, I know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Who is she related to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: She's -- her mother is on the list, too, Hata Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is she related to Huso Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, she's Huso's sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 26, Hasan Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: (redacted) We need a redaction at page 14 and line -- excuse me, 15, lines 1 through 3. Can we move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And can we move into private session for a couple questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, the Hasan Kurspahic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please comment on whether you know number 27, Hasiba Kurspahic, and whether she is alive?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Let's touch on number 28: Hasnija Kurspahic, approximately 62 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know her. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Has there ever been a Hasnija Kurspahic as far as you knew from Koritnik or the area where you were married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: There was a Hasnija Kurspahic, but she got married somewhere in Zepa, but she wasn't that old. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 29, Hata Kurspahic, approximately 68 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Hata Kurspahic is Hana's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 30, Ifeta Kurspahic, approximately 17 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. She had just gotten married into Koritnik. She has been in Koritnik for just a few months. I know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 31, Igabala Kurspahic, approximately 58 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. She was there. I know her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 32, Ismet Kurspahic, approximately 3 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Ismet Kurspahic is Dzehva's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 33: Ismeta Kurspahic, approximately 26 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Ismeta Kurspahic is mother of Aida, Almir, and Vahid. They were all still in Koritnik when I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 34, Izeta Kurspahic, approximately 24 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Izeta? I don't know anyone by the name of Izeta Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 35, Kada Kurspahic, approximately 40 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Kada Kurspahic. Do you mean Kada Sehic. She was married Sehic. She lived in Koritnik, Hana's sister and daughter of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat. Whose daughter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Daughter of whom, Witness? Would you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hata's daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so Kada's maiden name was Sehic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No. Her maiden name was Kurspahic, and her married name was Sehic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 39, Medena Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, I know her. She was in Koritnik when I left, Medo Kurspahic's daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So that's number 40, Medo Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so we're going on to number 43, Mina Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Mina Kurspahic, I don't know who that could be. There was only Jasmina Kurspahic, married name Delija.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So do you believe that Mina Kurspahic is a duplicate of Jasmina Delija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know. I just didn't know anyone by the name of Mina Kurspahic. There was a Jasmina. I don't know if that's the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it common for Jasminas to be called Mina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 44, Mirela Kurspahic, approximately 3 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Mirela Kurspahic was the daughter of Dzehva Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 45, Mujesira Kurspahic, approximately 35 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Mujesira Kurspahic, mother of Enisa Kurspahic. She stayed in Koritnik when I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 46, Munevera Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, I know her, Alija Kurspahic's daughter. She stayed in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 47, Munira Kurspahic, approximately 12 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know anyone named Munira, 12 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 48, Munira Kurspahic, approximately 55 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: That's the mother of Munevera Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 49, Osman Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: That's the father-in-law of Ismeta Kurspahic. He stayed behind me in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 50, Pasana or Pasija Kurspahic, approximately 56 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. Pasija Kurspahic was Edhem's wife, wife of Edhem Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you believe that number 28, Hasnija Kurspahic, is a duplicate of Pasija or Pasana Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No. No. It could only be Pasija's daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 51, Ramiza Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Ramiza Kurspahic is wife of Becar Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know if she was alive or in Koritnik when you departed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 52, Sabiha Kurspahic, approximately 14 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Sabiha is Hasan Kurspahic's daughter. She stayed in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 53, Sadeta Kurspahic, approximately 18.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. She had a 2-year -- 2-day-old baby. She stayed in Koritnik. She was pregnant when I left, but you could see she was with-child as I was leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 54, Safa Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Safa Kurspahic, wife of Medo Kurspahic. She stayed behind me in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 55, Saha Kurspahic, approximately 70 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Saha Kurspahic, it could only be Hasa if she were younger. I don't know Saha or Saha.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 56, Sajma Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Sajma was Hasan Kurspahic's daughter. She stayed in Koritnik when I left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Of course it could be, but the age does not correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you didn't know any other child with that name approximately 2 years old?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I did not know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 59, Sumbula Kurspahic, approximately 62 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, I know her. She was in Koritnik as I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 60, Vahid Kurspahic, approximately 8 years old.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know Vahid Kurspahic. He's Ismet Kurspahic's son.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 61, Fazila Memisevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Memisevic. I know her. She stayed behind me in Koritnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Redzo Memisevic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Redzo Memisevic, Fazila's husband. He also stayed in Koritnik as I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you. Number 63, Rabija Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Rabija Sadikovic, I know her. She lived in Pionirska Street. That's a neighbour of Jasmina Delija. Jasmina lived in Rabija's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 64, Enver Sehic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Enver Sehic, I know him. He's a son of Kada Sehic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 65, Faruk Sehic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Faruk Sehic is Enver's brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we need a redaction at page 52, line 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And number 66, Haraga Sehic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, where were the Sehics living at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: They were at Musici, this family.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 67, Kada Sehic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Kada Sehic is Faruk and Enver's mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you believe that this is a duplicate of number 35, Kada Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Number 68, Nurka Velic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I really don't know that woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know a Tima Velic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know Tima Velic either.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know Jasmina Vila?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know her, but I heard of her as being from Musici. I heard of such a girl, but I'd never met her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am, for coming to court and taking this stress on your life, I apologise again, really, for your troubles, and go well with your life, ma'am. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, my name is Dermot Groome, and I'm one of the Prosecutors on the case. I will refer to you by CW1, as well, to protect your identity. My first question to you is, you've gone through a list of names, and you've mentioned quite a few of them that you know. Aside from the ones that we've discussed in closed session, the ones with an immediate relationship to you, how many have you seen since June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: As far as I know, I've seen all the Kurspahics in Koritnik. When I left they were all alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What I'm asking you now is, just looking at your passport when it was passed around to me, it seemed that there were a number of endorsements showing that you had returned to Bosnia, so my question is, on your visits back to Bosnia, have you seen anyone on that list, or has anyone on that list ever come to visit you in Austria?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes, I did go. Of course, I went to Visegrad and to Sarajevo. However, I never met any one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the Defence has claimed that some of these people are in fact still living, and we are continuing to investigate those claims, and it would be helpful if you were able to provide a bit of additional information on the people that you know. And the first person I want to ask you about is the person who's number 4, Jasmina Delija. Do you know the name of her father and her mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know. I know. I'll tell you gladly. Safet Kurspahic is her father. Bisera Kurspahic is her mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you happen to know the year of birth of Jasmina Delija?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but she's the generation of 1967, but you have to check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, there is a group of people on the list all having the family name of Jasarevic that you said you did not know. Recognising that you did not recognise -- or you did not know the names of these people, were you familiar with any other villages in Visegrad where there were people of the name Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, really. I couldn't. I had no contact with anyone named Jasarevic. I don't know anyone from that family.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that we go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam, on number 22 on the list was a person by the name of Hasa Kurspahic, who you said that you knew her. Could I ask her, do you know her mother and her father's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Hasan Kurspahic was her father, and her mother's name was Mejra. I believe the woman's name is Hasa, with a diacritic on the S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, number 32 on the list was a person you said you knew, Ismet Kurspahic. Again, could I ask you if you know the father and the mother of Ismet Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. Kurspahic, Dzheva, and the father was Fehret Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On that, Mr. Groome, if you go to number 60, Vahid Kurspahic, approximately 8 years old, and the witness told Mr. Alarid, I believe, that he was the son of Ismet Kurspahic. Was that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His mother is Ismeta, and his father is Hidajit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise. Could we go back into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam, I want to ask you about the Pionirska Street area, and you've already told us where you live, so please don't make any reference to where you live in open session. Did you know a couple by the name of Sevko and Rasima Kurspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam, can I ask you, all of these people that you mentioned, do they all hail from the same extended Kurspahic family from Koritnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any other areas in the town centre that people from Koritnik -- that Kurspahics from Koritnik went and lived? Or were they all kind of in the particular area of town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: There was a family in Srnice, Ramo Kurspahic with his family, and there weren't any more of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So aside from Ramo Kurspahic, all the Kurspahics that moved to town from Koritnik all lived in the Pionirska Street area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: The first ones that I mentioned, yes; Ramo, though, was in Srnice across the Drina River. He was in the Alhos company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, madam, while we're talking about some of the people from the Kurspahic family that you know, I had asked that you be shown Prosecution Exhibit 61. It is all of the photographs that we were able to gather about the family. Did you have an opportunity to look through them while -- over the break?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you recognise some of the people in those photographs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Mostly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you be handed back that stack of photographs. I think probably the most efficient way for us to do this is if we could use the ELMO, and could I ask you to place the photo of the people that you recognise on the ELMO so that all of us can see it with the assistance of the usher. And if you could tell us who you recognise in this photograph from P61.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Ifeta Kurspahic, who is married to Dzevad Kurspahic, is on this photograph, and she's the daughter-in-law of Becar Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there any photograph -- the photograph on the reverse of that page, do you recognise that person?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you tell us which people you recognise here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I know only Jesira Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is she one of the people that you gave evidence of earlier today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that you hand the usher the next photo, if there are any, that you recognise the people in the photograph as being people that you've testified -- and you've already testified about today.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In the stack of photographs, if you would indicate to the usher which of the photographs you do recognise, and then she'll place it on the ELMO, on the projector next to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Again, this is a photograph from P61. Who is it that you recognise on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I recognise Osman Kurspahic and his grandson Vahid Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just -- I apologise for interrupting, but to clarify the record, could we indicate which number the photograph is as we're going through? I know -- because you're saying just a photograph from P61, but it might help clean up the record if we refer to the number of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. This is photograph number 4 from P61.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you've given your evidence about that. Could I ask whether you recognise any of the people on the reverse of this photograph, the reverse of this page, and that is picture number 5. Did you know this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, I do not recognise the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you to hand the usher the next photograph that contains a picture of a person that you recognise and have testified about here today. If it could be brought down just for a second so I could see the number at the top. Okay, this is number 12. Can I ask you who you recognise in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Kada Kurspahic is shown on the photograph. Her married name is Sehic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you recognise any of the people depicted on the back of that photograph? That's photograph 11.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Yes. Bula Kurspahic. Just one moment. Not Bula but Hata. Hata Kurspahic; Ramiza Kurspahic, Becar's wife; this grandmother here is the mother of Hasan Kurspahic, but I don't know her name. I recognise her, though. As for the others, I don't know who they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you to hand the next photograph that contains someone that you recognise and have testified about here today. Again, if I could just see -- this is photograph number 3. Who do you recognise in photograph 3 from P61?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Osman Kurspahic, Aida Kurspahic, Almir Kurspahic, Ajka Kurspahic, and Ismeta Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask the usher maybe to flip it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise the people on the reverse of the photo, and if I could just see the top corner for just a second. It's number 2 in P61.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Rabija Sadikovic and the children, Haris and Mirsada.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any more of the photographs that I asked you to look at over the break that you know the people depicted in them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Kada Kurspahic again. Her married name is Sehic; and Kada's father, Asim Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how about the reverse of that sheet? Do you recognise anyone there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Just so the record is complete, you did not recognise the person depicted on photograph 1 of P61. Do you recognise anyone in the remaining photographs that you have on the desk before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: On this photograph as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that's photograph 8.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Bula Kurspahic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if I could ask the usher to please turn the photograph over. This is 9.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dzheva Kurspahic, Mirela, and Mirela's -- Dzheva's husband, Fehret.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, could ask that photograph number 11 be placed back up on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could we have a redaction, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There are a few questions that I want to ask you with respect to your efforts to get a permit to leave. You mentioned that you went to the police station several times in order to try to secure a permit to leave. How many times altogether did you go to the Visegrad police station to try to get that permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I was there on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, and I received it on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the days that you were unsuccessful in getting that permit, were you told why you could not get it on those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: There were many of us all the time. We were all waiting for documents, and then we were told the time has run out and you need to go home and come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you explain to the Chamber, what was the procedure and what was the purpose of needing some kind of paper to actually leave the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Well, what do I know? Wherever we wanted to go at the border crossing, they would ask us for this pass, whether we had received a permit from the SUP to leave town. That's why I went, to ask for that permit, and on Friday I got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the procedure? Were you asked questions? Did you have to produce documents? What was the procedure that was involved in securing such a permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Of course there was a procedure. They asked me where I wanted to go. I said my husband's family is in Belgrade. I wanted to go there. How long do you want to stay? I said, About two months, until everything blows over. And that was it. They would write down my name and surname, my ID card number, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned at least on one of these days you saw a person you knew as Milan Lukic. Which of the days in the week was it that you saw Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly whether it was the Monday or the Tuesday, but one of those two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was it only on the one day of the week that you saw him there, or did you see him on other days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I didn't see him other times, just that day, that one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you said in your direct examination that he was there with a group. Could I ask you, how many people were in -- how many people were among the people you thought were in a group with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. I just turned around and saw them walking, and then he started yelling at us immediately. There were three or four or five men with him. I looked down like we all did, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you, what made you think that they were together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Well, I saw them walking together. I don't know whether they were really together, but they had come together in front of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've described how he was dressed when you saw him. Was there anything notable about the other people that you saw with him with respect to how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No. I did not notice anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the other people in his group at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, I didn't really because I didn't dare look them over. As soon as he came up and started yelling, I sort of shrank and looked down and hid my face.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, at some point you relayed to us a conversation you had with him. Could I ask you to tell us as precisely as you're able what it was you said to him and what it was he said to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: As we were standing in that queue, me must have recognised me. He took me by the arm and said, What's your business here? He called me schoolmate or neighbor or something. I said I came for a pass out of Visegrad. And he said, Where do you want to go? (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Don't answer it. Don't answer the question. Next question, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just simply asking what she believed it meant. I'm not asking her to speculate what he meant but simply what she believed given all the circumstances. She's talked about the aggressive nature, the angry way he presented himself to her. I believe I'm entitled to ask her how she perceived what he meant when he said not leave an ear standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, in the context of the circumstances surrounding the events of those days and this conversation with Mr. Milan Lukic, what did you understand him to mean when he said he had orders not to leave an ear of the Kurspahic family standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: How else could I understand it? The worst, that we are not going to be anymore. I was seized by fear that he would kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you believe him to mean that he intended or had orders to kill the entire Kurspahic family?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not allowing that. She has already told -- given you an answer. I think you have to take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When he made his statement any ear of a Kurspahic, did you understand that to mean not only men but of women, children, and elderly people from the Kurspahic family?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I don't think you can take it any further. I think the answer is very clear. We'll have to make up our minds on the basis of the answer that she has given as to what was meant by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say who it was that gave him orders to do this to the Kurspahic family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: I didn't ask him, and he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've described him wearing a police uniform. Did you believe him to be working for the police at the time he made this statement to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, I didn't think anything of the kind. I didn't even know what were police uniforms as opposed to army uniforms. All I knew was what I could see, that he had a dark blue uniform; but what it represented, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When he said "we," what did you understand him to mean when he was saying "we"? Who were the people that you believe he was referring to when he said "we"?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, she can answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said that he said we have orders not to leave an ear of the Kurspahic family standing. When you say "we," who did you understand him to mean when he said "we"? Obviously he's talking about more than simply himself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Of course. He knows what he meant. I don't know. All I could think was that's the end of us Kurspahics. I don't know what he meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to seeing him on this day, did you know him before this day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, I did not, except for those times at school when we ran into each other, but he was younger than me. But we hailed from neighboring villages, and somehow we recognised each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's the point I'm getting at. When you had a conversation with him on this day, you recognised him as being Milan Lukic, someone you knew before; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Naturally. Clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from knowing him from school and from the villages, was there any other context in which you knew Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: No, no. I really didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you feel you would be able to recognise him today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to take a look around the courtroom and tell us whether you recognise the person you've been referring to as the Milan Lukic in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Shall I stand up?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And simply, Your Honour, usual objection as to in-court ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ma'am, if you feel -- I'd like you to look at everyone in the courtroom carefully. If you feel you need to stand up to do that, please let me know, and I'll ask Judge Robinson if he'll allow you to stand up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. If you wish to stand, you may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Madam, you've made a gesture. We have to be very clear on the record what everything means. What did you mean with that gesture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to show you with my hand who I meant. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, that's perfectly fine. Could I ask you to, perhaps so the record is clear, you're looking to the left of the courtroom. There are three rows in the left-hand side of the courtroom. Can you tell us which row the person you recognise as Milan Lukic is sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: The last row. There are two men on his right-hand side and one man on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, I want to ask you, is it your right-hand side or his right-hand side? Perhaps if you do it from your --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: On his, on Milan's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Could I ask you -- I'm still not clear. Maybe if you count from the -- there's four people in that last row. Counting from the left, including all four people on the last row, which is the person that you're referring to? If I'd ask you to look at the last row so there is no mistaking which person you're referring to. Counting from the left, your left, which of the four people in that row is the person you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS CW1
utterances.text: To my left there is a policeman, if I can put it that way, then Milan, then Sredoje, then another policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that CW1 has identified Mr. Milan Lukic in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's all the questions that I had prepared for today. We were provided just not too long ago with a tape recording of some three hours. It was discoverable material. I've asked someone to be listening to it while I was here in court. They've gotten through about the first 50 minutes, but already I know that there's important questions that will be generated from that. The most important that I've heard so far is that there is -- part of the interview that was conducted with this woman, there's a discussion about another person with the exact same first and family name as this person, so I'm asking to have an opportunity this evening to listen to the tape, and I would ask that CW1, if we could impose upon her to just to take a few more questions from me tomorrow morning that would arise out of me listening to the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It would be in the afternoon. I believe we have changed to the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was unaware of that, Your Honour, but I think I could deal with it in 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll allow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, Your Honour, I won't -- I rest my cross-examination now, but those are the questions that I have for the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And Your Honour, could we have this discussion outside the witness, since she's still under oath and obviously being excused for the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 18th day of March, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.28 p.m.,
